The '''2012–13 Premier League''' (known as the '''[[Barclays]] Premier League''' for sponsorship reasons) was the 21st season of the [[Premier League]], the English professional league for association football clubs, since its establishment in 1992, and the 114th season of top-flight English football overall. The fixture schedule was released on 18 June 2012.<ref name="=Fixtures out on Monday">{{cite web |url=http://www.manutd.com/en/News-And-Features/Features/2012/Jun/video-fixtures-released-on-monday.aspx|date=16 June 2012 |title=Fixtures out on Monday |work=manutd.com|access-date=17 June 2012}}</ref><ref name="=When does the 2012/13 season start?">{{cite web|url=http://www.premierleague.com/en-gb/fans/faqs/when-does-2012-13-season-start.html |title=When does the 2012/13 season start? |work=premierleague.com |publisher=Premier League |date=8 May 2012 |access-date=15 May 2012 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120419211034/http://www.premierleague.com/en-gb/fans/faqs/when-does-2012-13-season-start.html |archive-date=19 April 2012 }}</ref> The season began on 18 August 2012 and ended on 19 May 2013.<ref name="=When does the 2012/13 season start?"/>

[[Manchester City F.C.|Manchester City]] were the defending champions, having won their first Premier League title the [[2011–12 Premier League|previous season]]. This was their first top division title [[List of English football champions|league title]] since the [[1967–68 in English football|1967–68]] season.

[[Manchester United F.C.|Manchester United]] secured their 13th Premier League title with four games to spare with a 3–0 win over [[Aston Villa F.C.|Aston Villa]] on 22 April 2013. Their 20th English title overall, this left defending champions Manchester City, who suffered a 3–1 defeat to [[Tottenham Hotspur F.C.|Tottenham Hotspur]] a day earlier, trailing 16 points behind their [[Manchester derby|local rivals]] with only five matches left to play.<ref>{{cite news|url= https://www.theguardian.com/football/2013/apr/23/alex-ferguson-robin-van-persie-goal|title= Sir Alex Ferguson hails Robin van Persie's 'goal of the century'|date=22 April 2013|work=Guardian UK|access-date=23 April 2013|location=London|first=Jamie|last=Jackson}}</ref> It was the first time the title had been decided in April since Chelsea were the winners in [[2005–06 FA Premier League|2005–06]], and only the fourth time in the history of the Premier League that it had been won with at least four games remaining in the season since [[Arsenal F.C.|Arsenal]] won in [[2003–04 FA Premier League|2003–04]].{{citation needed|date=July 2020}} [[England national football team manager]] [[Roy Hodgson]] declared that United manager [[Alex Ferguson|Sir Alex Ferguson]] was a "magician" having won 13 titles in 21 seasons.<ref>{{cite web | url = https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/22268871| title = Sir Alex Ferguson is a magician, says England boss Roy Hodgson | publisher = BBC Sport| access-date = 23 April 2013 | date = 23 April 2013}}</ref> On 8 May 2013, Ferguson announced his retirement; his final game in charge was away to [[West Bromwich Albion F.C.| West Bromwich Albion]] on the final day of the season, which ended in a 5–5 draw.

On 28 April 2013, [[Queens Park Rangers F.C.|Queens Park Rangers]] and [[Reading F.C.|Reading]] were both relegated from the Premier League after a goalless draw against each other.<ref>{{cite web | url = https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/22237302| title = Reading 0–0 QPR | publisher = BBC Sport| access-date = 28 April 2013 | date = 28 April 2013}}</ref> [[Wigan Athletic F.C.|Wigan Athletic]] were the third and final club to be relegated, following a 4–1 defeat to Arsenal on 14 May 2013. This brought an end to their eight-year stay in the Premier League, and came just three days after winning the [[2012–13 FA Cup|season's FA Cup]], making them the first club to win the [[FA Cup]] and suffer relegation in the same season.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/22430454| title = Arsenal 4–1 Wigan | publisher = BBC Sport| access-date = 14 May 2013 | date = 14 May 2013}}</ref>

An independent commission later [[Manchester City F.C. financial breaches scandal|found that Manchester City breached Premier League financial rules]] during this season, part of a pattern of breaches spanning 2009-2018.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2026-09-29 |title=Premier League statement in full as Man City guilty of ‘sham’ deals and other charges |url=https://www.independent.co.uk/sport/football/man-city-guilty-premier-league-statement-full-charges-b3058442.html |access-date=2026-10-04 |website=The Independent |language=en}}</ref>

==Season summary==
The season opened the weekend of 18 August 2012. Defending champions [[Manchester City F.C.|Manchester City]] opened their season with a narrow 3–2 victory over [[Southampton F.C.|Southampton]], who had just been promoted back to the Premier League after seven seasons in lower divisions. Man City had taken a 1–0 lead, with Southampton turning it on its head to go 2–1 up with 20 minutes remaining. City eventually came back and [[Samir Nasri]] scored the winning goal with ten minutes left.<ref>{{cite web|title=Fixture: Man City vs. Southampton|url=http://www.premierleague.com/content/premierleague/en-gb/matchday/matches/2012-2013/epl.match-report.html/man-city-vs-southampton|work=Premier League official website|access-date=23 April 2013|date=19 August 2012|archive-date=29 July 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130729043559/http://www.premierleague.com/content/premierleague/en-gb/matchday/matches/2012-2013/epl.match-report.html/man-city-vs-southampton|url-status=dead}}</ref> In a Monday evening fixture at [[Goodison Park]], [[Manchester United F.C.|Manchester United]] started their season with a 1–0 loss to [[Everton F.C.|Everton]], the goal scored by [[Marouane Fellaini]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Fixture: Everton vs. Manchester United|url=http://www.premierleague.com/content/premierleague/en-gb/matchday/matches/2012-2013/epl.match-report.html/everton-vs-man-utd|date=20 August 2012|access-date=23 April 2013|archive-date=28 January 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130128091322/http://www.premierleague.com/content/premierleague/en-gb/matchday/matches/2012-2013/epl.match-report.html/everton-vs-man-utd|url-status=dead}}</ref> The first goal of the season, however, was scored by [[Swansea City F.C.|Swansea City]]'s [[Michu]],<ref name="Michu">{{cite web|title=Michu scores the first goal of the 2012/13 Premier League season|url=http://www.itv.com/sport/football/article/2012-08-18/michu-scores-the-first-goal-of-the-2012-13-premier-league-season/|work=ITV Sport|publisher=Independent Television (ITV)|date=18 August 2012|access-date=5 November 2012|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120822055506/http://www.itv.com/sport/football/article/2012-08-18/michu-scores-the-first-goal-of-the-2012-13-premier-league-season/|archive-date=22 August 2012|url-status=dead}}</ref> whose team thrashed [[Queens Park Rangers F.C.|Queens Park Rangers]] 5–0 away from home.<ref>{{cite news|title= The Joy of Six: Premier League opening-day debuts|first1=Nick|last1=Miller|first2=Nick|last2=Ames|first3=Michael|last3=Butler|date=10 August 2017|access-date=11 August 2017|work=The Guardian|url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/blog/2017/aug/10/the-joy-of-six-premier-league-opening-day-debuts}}</ref>

Manchester United recovered from their opening week loss with a 3–2 win over [[Fulham F.C.|Fulham]] in their opening home game at [[Old Trafford]], but lost striker [[Wayne Rooney]] to injury during the match.<ref>{{cite web|title=Fixture: Manchester United vs. Fulham|url=http://www.premierleague.com/content/premierleague/en-gb/matchday/matches/2012-2013/epl.match-report.html/man-utd-vs-fulham|date=25 August 2012|access-date=23 April 2013|archive-date=29 July 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130729050648/http://www.premierleague.com/content/premierleague/en-gb/matchday/matches/2012-2013/epl.match-report.html/man-utd-vs-fulham|url-status=dead}}</ref> Other second week highlights included [[Chelsea F.C.|Chelsea]]'s 2–0 win over [[Newcastle United F.C.|Newcastle United]], with recent Belgian signing [[Eden Hazard]] involved in both goals.<ref>{{cite web|title=Fixture: Chelsea vs. Newcastle|url=http://www.premierleague.com/content/premierleague/en-gb/matchday/matches/2012-2013/epl.match-report.html/chelsea-vs-newcastle|date=25 August 2012|access-date=24 April 2013|archive-date=9 May 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130509025018/http://www.premierleague.com/content/premierleague/en-gb/matchday/matches/2012-2013/epl.match-report.html/chelsea-vs-newcastle|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Hazard fires for Blues, RVP scores|url=http://espnfc.com/news/story/_/id/1142301/premier-league:-hazard-fires-for-blues,-rvp-scores?cc=5901|work=espnfc.com|access-date=23 April 2013|date=25 August 2012}}</ref>

Early leaders Chelsea had week three off, while a win by Manchester City over Queens Park Rangers left the defending champions two points off the pace. The game was a highly anticipated rematch between the two teams that squared off on the final day of the [[2011–12 Premier League|2011–12 season]], when Manchester City snatched the title on goal difference with a late goal by [[Sergio Agüero]]. This time though, it was less exciting, with Manchester City comfortably winning 3–1.<ref>{{cite web|title=Fixture: Man City vs. QPR United|url=http://www.premierleague.com/content/premierleague/en-gb/matchday/matches/2012-2013/epl.match-report.html/man-city-vs-qpr/everton-vs-man-utd|date=1 September 2012}}{{dead link|date=July 2013}}</ref> Level on points with Manchester City in second place were Swansea City, who registered a 2–2 draw with [[Sunderland A.F.C.|Sunderland]], and [[West Bromwich Albion F.C.|West Bromwich Albion]], who defeated Everton 2–0.<ref>{{cite web|title=City see off QPR|url=http://espnfc.com/news/story/_/id/1148480/premier-league:-man-city-beat-qpr,-norwich-deny-tottenham?cc=5901|work=espnfc.com|access-date=24 April 2013|date=1 September 2012}}</ref>

The fourth week of the season began with controversy, as the Chelsea v Queens Park Rangers match was fraught with racial tensions when QPR's [[Anton Ferdinand]] refused to shake hands with Chelsea's [[John Terry]], who had been suspended for four games for using racial epithets against Ferdinand during the previous season.<ref>{{cite web|title=Premier League mandates handshake|url=http://espnfc.com/news/story/_/id/1159110/premier-league-mandates-qpr,-chelsea-pre-match-handshake?cc=5901|work=espnfc.com|access-date=24 April 2013|date=14 September 2012}}</ref> The teams would play out a 0–0 draw, however second place Manchester City could not gain ground as they also drew, with [[Stoke City F.C.|Stoke City]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Stoke deny City|url=http://espnfc.com/news/story/_/id/1159728/prem:-stoke-deny-man-city,-arsenal-and-man-utd-cruise?cc=5901|work=espnfc.com|access-date=24 April 2013|date=14 September 2012}}</ref>

Week five saw Chelsea extend their league lead to 3 points with a 1–0 win over Stoke City. A late goal in the 85th minute by [[Ashley Cole]] secured the win for the Blues.<ref>{{cite web|title=Fixture: Chelsea vs. Stoke|url=http://www.premierleague.com/content/premierleague/en-gb/matchday/matches/2012-2013/epl.match-report.html/chelsea-vs-stoke|date=22 September 2012|access-date=24 April 2013|archive-date=20 May 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130520173504/http://www.premierleague.com/content/premierleague/en-gb/matchday/matches/2012-2013/epl.match-report.html/chelsea-vs-stoke|url-status=dead}}</ref> Everton and West Bromwich Albion maintained control of second place, with both teams notching a win in week five, though a draw by the Baggies in week six would drop them back to fifth place, which they would share with [[Tottenham Hotspur F.C.|Tottenham Hotspur]] following their surprise 3–2 win over Manchester United at Old Trafford. Chelsea, Everton, and Manchester City would all win in week six. The results table after six games would have Chelsea in the lead with 16 points, followed by Everton and Manchester City with 13 points each, and Manchester United with 12. At the bottom of the league, [[Liverpool F.C.|Liverpool]] forward [[Luis Suárez (Uruguayan footballer)|Luis Suárez]] scored a [[hat trick]] against [[Norwich City F.C.|Norwich City]], leading Liverpool to a 5–2 victory. It was the second consecutive year that Suárez had scored a hat trick at [[Carrow Road]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Spurs stun United, Chelsea sink Arsenal|url=http://www.espn.co.uk/football/sport/story/172425.html|work=espn.co.uk|access-date=24 April 2013|date=29 September 2012}}</ref>

The month of October saw a tightening at the top of the standings, with Chelsea, Manchester United and Manchester City all winning their first two of three games for the month, setting up a vital Sunday afternoon match at [[Stamford Bridge (stadium)|Stamford Bridge]] between third placed Manchester United and the leaders Chelsea. The game did not disappoint, as Chelsea went down 2–0 early on an [[own goal]] by [[David Luiz]] in the fourth minute and a goal by [[Robin van Persie]] in the 12th. Van Persie had also taken the shot that had rebounded off of Luiz, and thus was ultimately responsible for the Red Devil's one-goal lead at half-time, following a late first half goal by Chelsea's [[Juan Mata]] from a free kick. Eight minutes into the second half [[Ramires]] equalised for Chelsea, and in the 75th minute United's [[Javier Hernández]] scored what proved to be the deciding goal via a rebound from a missed Van Persie shot. Replays showed that Hernández was in an offside position, generating a great deal of controversy. After the game, only a single point separated leaders Chelsea from second placed Manchester United.<ref>{{cite web|title=Fixture: Chelsea vs. Man Utd|url=http://www.premierleague.com/content/premierleague/en-gb/matchday/matches/2012-2013/epl.match-report.html/chelsea-vs-man-utd|access-date=23 April 2013|date=28 October 2012|archive-date=29 July 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130729052333/http://www.premierleague.com/content/premierleague/en-gb/matchday/matches/2012-2013/epl.match-report.html/chelsea-vs-man-utd|url-status=dead}}</ref> The rest of the standings were tightly packed in mid-table as 4 points separated fourth through ninth place. Another key match in October included a fixture between Liverpool and Reading, with Liverpool winning 1–0 (with winger Raheem Sterling scoring his first goal for the club) and giving manager [[Brendan Rodgers]] his first win at [[Anfield]] in the league against Reading, a team he formerly managed.<ref>{{cite web|title=Liverpool's Raheem Sterling scores winner|url=http://espnfc.com/news/story/_/id/1195836/liverpool's-raheem-sterling-scores-winner-vs.-reading?cc=5901|work=espnfc.com|access-date=24 April 2013|date=20 October 2012}}</ref> The final week of October featured the longest match in the 20-year history of the Premier League, a 103-minute game between Manchester City and Swansea that featured two serious injuries, one to the groin of Swansea keeper [[Michel Vorm]] and the other to the knee of Manchester City back [[Micah Richards]], both of which required stretchers to carry them off. City prevailed 1–0 in the marathon event with a goal from [[Carlos Tevez]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Tevez piledriver silences Manchester City critics|url=http://www.espn.co.uk/football/sport/story/176533.html#|work=espn.co.uk|access-date=24 April 2013|date=27 October 2013}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Fixture: Man City vs. Swansea|url=http://www.premierleague.com/en-gb/matchday/matches/2012-2013/epl.match-preview.html/man-city-vs-swansea|access-date=23 April 2013|date=27 October 2012|archive-date=24 October 2012|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121024000841/http://www.premierleague.com/en-gb/matchday/matches/2012-2013/epl.match-preview.html/man-city-vs-swansea|url-status=dead}}</ref>

League leaders Chelsea suffered a dip in form in November. They opened the month with draws against Swansea City and Liverpool, dropping them to third in the standings. A loss to West Bromwich Albion on 17 November was marked by ineffective second half play, as the team was unable to capitalise on a late first half equaliser by Eden Hazard.<ref>{{cite web|title=Fixture: West Brom vs. Chelsea|url=http://www.premierleague.com/content/premierleague/en-gb/matchday/matches/2012-2013/epl.match-report.html/west-brom-vs-chelsea|access-date=24 April 2013|date=17 November 2012|archive-date=29 July 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130729051451/http://www.premierleague.com/content/premierleague/en-gb/matchday/matches/2012-2013/epl.match-report.html/west-brom-vs-chelsea|url-status=dead}}</ref> The Blues closed out the month with uninspiring 0–0 draws against Manchester City and Fulham. The primary beneficiaries of Chelsea's slide were Manchester United and Manchester City, as the two rivals moved into commanding control of the first two places in the league table. Key November games included a 2–1 Manchester United win over Arsenal on 3 November,<ref>{{cite web|title=Fixture: Man Utd vs. Arsenal|url=http://www.premierleague.com/content/premierleague/en-gb/matchday/matches/2012-2013/epl.match-report.html/man-utd-vs-arsenal|access-date=24 April 2013|date=3 November 2012|archive-date=19 July 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130719072712/http://www.premierleague.com/content/premierleague/en-gb/matchday/matches/2012-2013/epl.match-report.html/man-utd-vs-arsenal|url-status=dead}}</ref> and a dominating 5–0 win by Manchester City over [[Aston Villa F.C.|Aston Villa]] on 17 November marked by a pair of two-goal performances by Carlos Tevez and Sergio Aguero.<ref>{{cite web|title=Fixture: Man City vs. Aston Villa|url=http://www.premierleague.com/content/premierleague/en-gb/matchday/matches/2012-2013/epl.match-report.html/man-city-vs-aston-villa|access-date=24 April 2013|date=3 November 2012|archive-date=29 July 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130729053346/http://www.premierleague.com/content/premierleague/en-gb/matchday/matches/2012-2013/epl.match-report.html/man-city-vs-aston-villa|url-status=dead}}</ref> West Bromwich Albion proved to be the biggest mover up the league table, moving from eighth up to joint third with Chelsea, on the strength of four wins over Southampton, [[Wigan Athletic F.C.|Wigan Athletic]], Chelsea, and Sunderland. At the bottom end of the table, Queens Park Rangers found themselves as the only team without a league win by the end of November.

The month of December saw minimal change in the standings at the top end of the table. The situation by [[New Year's Eve]] with the top three places was the same as it was at the start of the month, though Manchester United had extended their lead over second place Manchester City to seven points, with Chelsea four points back from City in third place. Tottenham Hotspur occupied fourth place with Arsenal, Everton, and West Bromwich Albion all tied for fifth. Chelsea stopped their November slide with a 3–1 win at Sunderland on 8 December on the strength of two goals by [[Fernando Torres]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Fixture: Sunderland vs. Chelsea|url=http://www.premierleague.com/content/premierleague/en-gb/matchday/matches/2012-2013/epl.match-report.html/sunderland-vs-chelsea|access-date=24 April 2013|date=8 December 2012|archive-date=29 July 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130729053358/http://www.premierleague.com/content/premierleague/en-gb/matchday/matches/2012-2013/epl.match-report.html/sunderland-vs-chelsea|url-status=dead}}</ref> The [[Manchester derby]] was renewed on 9 December at the [[City of Manchester Stadium]] with first place on the line. United took a two-goal lead thanks to two goals from Wayne Rooney in the 16th and 30th minute. City responded with a [[Yaya Touré]] goal in the 60th minute, a goal that followed two saves in rapid succession by United keeper [[David de Gea]]. [[Pablo Zabaleta]] equalised in the 86th minute, but Robin van Persie once again proved to be the hero for United, scoring the winning goal two minutes into injury time to extend United's lead over City at the top of the table to six points.<ref>{{cite web|title=Fixture: Man City vs. Man Utd Villa|url=http://www.premierleague.com/content/premierleague/en-gb/matchday/matches/2012-2013/epl.match-report.html/man-city-vs-man-utd|access-date=24 April 2013|date=9 December 2012|archive-date=23 February 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130223043940/http://www.premierleague.com/content/premierleague/en-gb/matchday/matches/2012-2013/epl.match-report.html/man-city-vs-man-utd|url-status=dead}}</ref> The last team without a league win, Queens Park Rangers, finally got their first win of the season on 15 December.

==Teams==
Twenty teams competed in the league&nbsp;– the top seventeen teams from the previous season and the three teams promoted from the [[2011–12 Football League Championship|Championship]]. The promoted teams were [[Reading F.C.|Reading]], [[Southampton F.C.|Southampton]] and [[West Ham United F.C.|West Ham United]], returning to the top flight after absences of four years, seven years and one year respectively. They replaced [[Bolton Wanderers F.C.|Bolton Wanderers]], [[Blackburn Rovers F.C.|Blackburn Rovers]] (both teams relegated to the [[2012–13 Football League Championship|Championship]] after eleven years in the top flight) and [[Wolverhampton Wanderers F.C.|Wolverhampton Wanderers]] (ending their three-year top flight spell).

===Scoring===
* First goal of the season: [[Michu]] for Swansea City against Queens Park Rangers (<small>''18 August 2012''</small>)<ref name="Michu" />
* Fastest goal of the season: '''20 seconds''', [[Theo Walcott]] for Arsenal against Queens Park Rangers (<small>''4 May 2013''</small>)<ref>{{cite web|first=Chris|last=Bevan|title=Queens Park Rangers 0–1 Arsenal|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/22320618|work=BBC Sport|publisher=British Broadcasting Corporation |date=4 May 2013|access-date=9 May 2013}}</ref>
* Last goal of the season: [[Urby Emanuelson]] for Fulham against Swansea City, (<small>''19 May 2013''</small>)<ref>[https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/22499103 Sport&nbsp;– Swansea 0–3 Fulham<!-- Bot generated title -->]</ref>
* Largest winning margin: '''8 goals'''
**Chelsea 8–0 Aston Villa (<small>''23 December 2012''</small>)
* Highest scoring game: '''10 goals'''
**Arsenal 7–3 Newcastle United (<small>''29 December 2012''</small>)
**West Bromwich Albion 5–5 Manchester United (<small>''19 May 2013''</small>)
* Most goals scored in a match by a single team: '''8 goals'''
**Chelsea 8–0 Aston Villa (<small>''23 December 2012''</small>)
* Most goals scored in a match by a losing team: '''3 goals'''
**Reading 3–4 Manchester United (<small>''1 December 2012''</small>)
**Swansea City 3–4 Norwich City (<small>''8 December 2012''</small>)
**Manchester United 4–3 Newcastle United (<small>''26 December 2012''</small>)
**Norwich City 3–4 Manchester City (<small>''29 December 2012''</small>)
**Arsenal 7–3 Newcastle United (<small>''29 December 2012''</small>)
